method: static review of eslint-factory/src/rules/*.ts and *.test.ts (live lint blocked by sandbox)

findings.summary: Rule returns (accepts) whenever arguments.length >= 2, but parseInt(x, 0) and parseInt(x, undefined) still trigger implicit base detection (0x -> hex). A non-numeric-literal radix is also unchecked. Tests only cover radix 10.
Suggestion autofix emits `catch (err) { throw err; }`, a no-op rethrow that silences this rule while violating ESLint core `no-useless-catch` (recommended set) and adding zero handling.
findings.evidence: require-json-parse-try-catch.ts:161; asserted verbatim in test outputs

findings.summary: Bare `typeof err === 'object'` is accepted as a sufficient guard, but typeof null === 'object', so `err.status` after such a guard can throw on null/non-Error throws — exactly what the rule targets. Test at no-unsafe-catch-error-property.test.ts:348 asserts the null-unchecked form as valid.
